limitations_and_boundaries: Bistability without mechanosensing requires extreme fine-tuning of cellular tensions (σc 0.14–0.15), which would not ensure robustness given natural variabilities in myosin and tension levels.

Tension asymmetries ϵ in budded crypts are below the theoretical threshold required for organoids to stay within the budded or bistable region on lumen inflation, indicating additional mechanisms are needed.
The model assumes quasistatic conditions; inflation and myosin response occur in 15–30 min, faster than cell fate or lumen volume changes during morphogenesis.
The molecular mechanosensing mechanisms mediating feedback from crypt morphology to actomyosin localization remain unknown.
Further work needed to dissect whether additional feedback occurs on longer timescales (days) via cell fate maturation.
In vivo crypts may be subjected to other external forces (e.g., smooth muscle constriction, osmotic swelling of villus cells) not fully captured in the organoid model.
Theoretical analysis suggests similar bistability in open-tube geometries, but experimental validation in vivo is lacking.

methods.name: Theoretical modeling
methods.protocol_description: Minimal model of 3D epithelial monolayer shape with mechanosensitive feedback: crypt differential tension σc depends on intrinsic value σ and crypt radius of curvature Rc via σc = σ(Rc/˜R0)^(-n), where n is coupling strength. Lumen volume changes affect crypt geometry and tensions. Phase diagram computed for bulged vs. budded states.

study_units.name: Minimal model of organoid morphogenesis with mechanosensitive feedback

results.value_raw_text: Mechanosensing lowered the differential tension threshold for bistability and broadened the bistable region by an order of magnitude compared to without mechanosensing.
